text:
lina.sec: scanner flagged an image with a file named /app/.deploy_blob and a small .env in the same layer. quarantined the image.

lina.sec: image: gcr.io/redwood-staging/ingest@sha256:0b4c...

tom.build: copy that digest to private-ops, good catch. do not decrypt here.

vault-bot: Vault audit: secret written by ci-runner@redwood at 2025-08-11T09:14:02Z with metadata wrap_key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/pipeline/cryptoKeys/wrap-core

jason.sre: running `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` now to list who can decrypt wrap-core.

tom.build: likely cause: build step echoes wrapped blob into workspace and Dockerfile `COPY . /app` pulled it in. i'll audit build steps for the run id.

lina.sec: mitigation plan:
- rotate wrap key (create v2)
- create ephemeral rewrap service account with TTL and run rewrap job on artifacts in the CI window
- remove any stale principals from KMS IAM
- add build guard to fail if `*.wrap` or `*.env` files are in the build context

jason.sre: IAM shows principals: ci-runner@redwood (ok), deploy-bot@redwood (ok), old-builder@redwood (remove). will remove old-builder and post diff.

ci-bot: found 4 images built in the suspect window. attaching fingerprints to private-ops.

tom.build: i'll open PR for build guard and a post-build layer scan. tagging @lina.sec for fast review.

jason.sre: created wrap-core v2 and started a test rewrap for one blob: rewrap-job=rw-406789-1, output gs://redwood-secure/rewrap/test/. no errors so far. ETA full run ~30m.

lina.sec: enable a 1h deploy freeze for staging and prod to be safe. notify product if needed.

tom.build: deleting the quarantined staging image and any snapshots that reference it after we confirm no rollback needed. logged deleted digests in private-ops.

jason.sre: removed old-builder principal and granted rewrap-job SA decrypt permission with 2h TTL. posted IAM change.

lina.sec: once rewrap completes, paste audit summary here: rewrap job ids, new key version id, principals removed, images scrubbed, CI PR merged. will follow up with a short post-incident note. :lock:
